Hearts are actually a very rare organ in terms of transplants, people will be on heart transplant lists for months... Most usually end up dying before they receive a heart, So the donation boards are very strict regarding someone receiving a heart.

They want to ensure that the heart they are giving isn't wasted, So there are a lot of disqualifying factors, Age, they don't want to give you a new heart if you're just going to kick the bucket in a few years. Drinking/Drug habits. Terminal illness, or disease. And weight is a big one, for two reasons; One, if your overweight you're just going to ruin that heart anyways, and two, Overweight people having a higher chance of dying on the operating table.

Basically it's not very likely that a fatass is going to get your heart, maybe a valve if they can't use the whole thing, or a kidney or something. but rarely if ever a heart.

Organ donation is a shitlords game anyway. People in good shape (relatively speaking, some are quite underweight from illness of course), those who don't drink or smoke, no drug history or very limited, younger, they all factor into where and if you get on the list.
A ham might get an organ like a kidney but because of the prevalence of obesity and the like, hearts are often unusable even if they specify they are a donor. They also have different ratings of organs. For instance a ham might be eligible to receive a "C" grade kidney but an A or B would go to someone healthier. There are a lot of factors. Most fatasses though won't even be eligible to be on the list. It's throwing it away on a surgery that is already complicated. I mean, fatties have a higher risk of death from anesthesia, especially for such a long operation, and especially for someone who is in organ failure. Also known to not take medications accurately which is needed for post organ transplant, etc. High blood sugar will ruin a nice new organ as will high triglycerides. Too many bad factors against success, making them ineligible in almost every case

And keep in mind if you are a healthy individual, your organs can go on to save EIGHT people's lives, separately, and tissue and things can be used for around 50 people, to improve their lives, everything from burn victims to helping someone see again.
You can specify VERY specifically how you want your organs distributed.

But the apathetic majority has potential to save so many people.
